articles.summary: Liquid biopsy is a blood-based approach that analyzes circulating tumor DNA, or ctDNA, shed by cancer cells into the bloodstream. In oncology practice, ctDNA-based testing can provide timely molecular information when tissue is limited, unavailable, or difficult to obtain and is increasingly used as a complement to tissue-based testing in advanced cancer.1-³

articles.summary: The limitations of traditional oncology trial design are well understood. Histology-based enrollment strategies, while operationally straightforward, frequently obscure the underlying molecular heterogeneity that governs therapeutic response. As a result, many late-stage failures may not reflect an absence of drug activity, but rather, an inability to resolve biologically distinct patient subsets within a single trial population.

articles.summary: The 2026 ACC/AHA Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia introduced substantial changes to cardiovascular risk assessment and lipid management. Key updates include the adoption of the PREVENT atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk calculator, restoration of LDL cholesterol (LDL-C) and non-HDL cholesterol (non-HDL-C) treatment goals, expanded use of apolipoprotein B (apoB), universal lipoprotein(a) (Lp[a]) testing in adulthood, and a greater emphasis on reducing lifetime exposure to atherogenic lipoproteins.
articles.title: 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline update: Key recommendations for laboratory reporting and clinical interpretation

articles.summary: Identifying patients at risk for type 2 diabetes (T2D) before irreversible metabolic damage occurs can be challenging, as traditional markers (e.g., fasting glucose, HbA1c) often miss early dysfunction. Many patients progress rapidly,1 and by the time glycemic thresholds are crossed, significant β-cell function may already be lost.2,3 The Diabetes Risk Index (DRI) helps close this gap by detecting risk earlier, before changes in glucose levels become clinically apparent.
articles.title: Diabetes Risk Index (DRI): Stratifying risk independent of glycemic status
